title: Competing Extended-$s$- and $d$-Wave Pairing from Distinct Spin-Fluctuation Channels in Stoichiometric $\mathrm{FeTe}$
authors: Yichen Hua, Wen-lin Yang, Jian-Jian Miao, Hu Xu, Changming Yue
abstract: The recent observation of superconductivity in stoichiometric $\mathrm{FeTe}$ raises the question of how pairing develops in this tetragonal 11-type chalcogenide once interstitial Fe is removed. We construct an experimentally constrained five-orbital tight-binding model from first-principles calculations and treat electronic correlations and pairing within the fluctuation-exchange approximation. The linearized Eliashberg equation yields competing extended-$s$- and $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave spin-singlet pairing instabilities. Near stoichiometric filling, spin fluctuations near $(π,0)$ and $(0,π)$ in the unfolded one-Fe Brillouin zone connect the $Γ/M$ hole pockets with the $X/Y$ electron pockets and favor an extended-$s$ gap that changes sign between the hole and electron sheets. Upon electron doping, depletion of the hole pockets shifts the dominant scattering toward the $X$--$Y$ channel near $(π,π)$, making the $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state the leading instability, with nodal lines that avoid most of the Fermi surface. The relative strengths of the two pairing channels vary with filling and interaction strength as the dominant spin-fluctuation channel changes. Under matched interaction strength, temperature, and filling, the extended-$s$ eigenvalue is larger in $\mathrm{FeTe}$ than in $\mathrm{FeSe}$ throughout the range considered, while the $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave eigenvalue is also generally larger, particularly under electron doping. These results give concrete gap structures against which spectroscopic measurements of stoichiometric $\mathrm{FeTe}$ can be compared.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the superconducting pairing mechanism in $\mathrm{FeTe}$ using a five-orbital tight-binding model and the FLEX approximation. It reveals a strong competition between extended-$s$-wave and $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing symmetries. The favored symmetry switches depending on the doping level, providing concrete gap structures for comparison with spectroscopic measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates the competing superconducting pairing symmetries (extended-$s$-wave vs. $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave) in stoichiometric and doped $\mathrm{FeTe}$.
main_result: The dominant pairing symmetry is highly dependent on doping: extended-$s$-wave is favored near stoichiometry, while $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave becomes leading upon electron doping.
method: The pairing instabilities are determined by solving the linearized Eliashberg equation within the fluctuation-exchange (FLEX) approximation.
model_or_system: The study uses an experimentally constrained five-orbital tight-binding model for the tetragonal 11-type chalcogenide $\mathrm{FeTe}$. Electronic correlations are treated via a local Hubbard-Kanamori interaction Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Pairing tendency ($\lambda$), gap function ($\Delta(\mathbf{k})$), and spin/charge susceptibilities ($\hat{\chi}_{\mathrm{C/S}}(\mathbf{q})$).
important_parameters: Doping level ($n$), interaction strength ($U$), and momentum transfer vectors $\mathbf{q}$ near $(\pi, 0)$, $(0, \pi)$, and $(\pi, \pi)$.
main_assumptions: The model neglects interlayer hoppings along the z-direction, and the pairing is analyzed within the spin-singlet channel approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Fermi surface topology, spin susceptibility peaks related to nesting vectors, and the calculated gap functions for different doping regimes.
paper_structure: The work proceeds by constructing a tight-binding model, applying the FLEX approximation to calculate spin fluctuations, and then solving the Eliashberg equation to map out the competing $s$-wave and $d$-wave pairing instabilities as a function of doping.
why_interesting: While focused on iron pnictides, the methodology of using fluctuation-exchange theory to map out competing pairing symmetries based on Fermi surface nesting is a general technique for understanding unconventional superconductivity in correlated electron systems.
